topology_reference.purpose: identify sampled endpoints by country index; does not infer visible geometry from the adjacency table

observations.statement: The full board view shows pale, approximately straight strokes spanning water gaps between the country-bearing island silhouettes. Ownership tint changes country fills; strokes are distinguishable against blue water. Relief texture and contrasting borders help land/water separation.
observations.confidence: high for this inspected image; not a general perceptual study

observations.statement: Short crossing 26–27 is isolated at the upper right; the two small country-index circles beside the contacts disambiguate its ends. Diagonal 1–13 contacts the upper country of the middle-left island, above neighbouring country 12; country labels and stroke continuation to shore support the reading.
observations.confidence: high visual interpretation with F017 adjacency cross-check; not evidence that players always perceive it correctly

observations.statement: The lower cluster has a longer slanted 43–44 link with endpoints near textured country margins. The nearly vertical 23–38 stroke ends beside a multi-country island; without country labels/table context, nearby countries are plausible visual alternatives. The view is a fixed layout, not a demonstrated general routing algorithm.
observations.confidence: moderate visual interpretation; ambiguity is an observer judgment, not measured player error

observations.statement: No crossing in the selected examples needs a curved detour across the visible water span. Exact full-path endpoints under land artwork, minimum clearance to all unrelated coasts, line-shape construction, and any coastline midpoint rule are not established.
observations.confidence: high for visible sampled straight spans; unknown beyond them

observations.statement: The placement frame has an arrow beside country 2 and a bottom-panel selected-country identifier. BehaviorScript 400 placement/move branches position sprite 130 at fixed country coordinates; the phase scripts show/hide/reset it. This is selected-country feedback, not proof of a legal-neighbour overlay.

The same-run combat-ready/result images identify defender country 1 and attacking country 2 in the bottom panel, with counts updated after exchange. They do not show a newly highlighted set of legal neighbours or altered crossing strokes. The examined click handler checks ownership and adjacency and writes identifiers/refusals; it contains no neighbour-wide highlighting loop in those branches.
observations.confidence: high for sampled same-island exchange; general absence remains unestablished

observations.statement: This recorded attack is within one island. It does not establish runtime feedback when selecting across water, target-selection intermediate frames, all legal/illegal inputs, keyboard behaviour, or all UI phases.
